newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Nov consumer prices up 3.19 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Nov consumer prices up 3.19 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's consumer prices in November rose 3.19 percent compared to November 1995, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Thursday.
On a month-to-month basis, the November consumer price index was down 0.07 percent from October, the directorate said.
At the wholesale level, November wholesale prices were down 3.02 percent compared to November 1995 and down 0.41 percent from October 1996, it said.
Between January and November, consumer prices rose an average 3.12 percent from the same period in 1995, slightly higher than the directorate's most recent forecast.
That forecast, issued in November, said prices would rise a year-on-year 3.1 percent for all of 1996.
November food prices fell 1.06 percent from October due to abundant supplies in the current peak season for vegetables and meat, the directorate said.
Prices for clothing rose 4.33 percent from October as winter apparel hit the market, it said.
Import prices fell 4.52 percent from a year earlier while export prices fell 1.58 percent, it said.
